interactions.summary: Jiang completes his community explanation by saying the school's flattened community is made up of what he calls learners.
The interviewer begins closing the conversation, apologizes for coughing, and says he wants to keep building the project through later panel discussions with more educators.
Jiang replies that empathy is still completely new in China, that promoting it is an uphill battle, and that any allies are valuable.
The interview ends with thanks, agreement to follow up by email, and a friendly exchange over names before goodbye.
The video closes by repeating the empathy slogan from the opening bumper.

speaker_notes.note: This goodbye segment mixes Edwin, Rebecca, and Jiang as they exchange thanks and pronunciation corrections.

claims.claim: Jiang names the school's community not as a hierarchy of fixed roles but as a community of learners.
The interviewer says he wants the next step to be a panel discussion with additional school participants, extending the conversation into a wider empathy network.
Jiang says empathy is completely new in China and that promoting it there is an uphill battle.
Jiang says outside allies matter because the effort to promote empathy in China cannot be carried by the school alone.
The closing bumper defines empathy as a quality of character that can change the world.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang's anti-hierarchical school model resolves into one compact label: learners.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the school's flattened social ideal a memorable name.

signature_moments.moment: The interview closes on a sober diagnosis: empathy is still new in China and every ally counts because the climb is uphill.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This line condenses the difficulty, novelty, and coalition logic behind Jiang's whole project.

signature_moments.moment: The closing bumper returns the interview to its framing slogan about seeing through other people's eyes.
signature_moments.source_phrase: See the world through other people's eyes
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It bookends the interview and makes empathy sound like a perceptual discipline with world-changing stakes.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's label for a school community in which administrators, teachers, assistants, and students are all participants in one learning collective rather than rigid status tiers.

chronology_notes.note: This final packet closes the 2012 interview with future-oriented plans for follow-up panels and email coordination, while Jiang restates the broader national difficulty of the empathy project.
